key_insight: The paper minimizes Mean Age of Incorrect Information (MAoII) in pull-based remote estimation of a Markov source by optimizing when the monitor should request samples under delay and sampling-rate constraints.
engineering_relevance: It provides a principled control policy for freshness-critical remote monitoring systems where outdated or wrong state estimates can directly affect decision-making.
method: Formulate the zero-delay case as a semi-Markov decision process to obtain an optimal observation-dependent pull policy.
For unit-delay channels, compute MAoII and average sampling rate numerically using the joint age-source distribution from the full observation history (belief).
Use a belief-MDP with constrained deep reinforcement learning to learn a belief-dependent pull policy under sampling constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical optimization for the zero-delay model and numerical evaluation plus algorithmic development for the unit-delay model, including computation of MAoII and average sampling rate.
watch_item: The unit-delay setting relies on belief-state estimation and deep RL, which may be computationally heavy and sensitive to approximation error or model mismatch.
paper_title: Minimizing Age of Incorrect Information in Pull-Based Remote Estimation of a Markov Source
